This notebook reads a run folder written by the
[prepare-and-run notebook](palace_eigenmode_bands_prepare_run.qmd), after the
run returns, on this machine or from a cluster. It needs no layout, mesh or
Palace.

## Returned Run

Set the two values the prepare-and-run notebook printed. The handoff ID
proves the folder is the run that notebook prepared.

```{python}
#| id: band-analyze-inputs
from pathlib import Path

from IPython.display import display
from scgsim.palace import inspect_run_trustworthiness, resolve_palace_result

RETURNED_RUN_DIR = Path("<run_dir printed by the prepare-and-run notebook>")
EXPECTED_HANDOFF_ID = "<handoff_id printed by the prepare-and-run notebook>"
```

## Run Status and Convergence

This report also reads a run that stopped early: which passes finished, how
the frequency moved between them, and how long each took.

```{python}
#| id: band-analyze-trust
report = inspect_run_trustworthiness(RETURNED_RUN_DIR)
display(report.show_run_trustworthiness(show_details=True))
display(report.show_simulation_benchmark(show_details=True))
```

## Surface EPR by Band

Only a completed run resolves; an unfinished one stops here with the reason.
The physics report lists each surface's whole participation, then splits the
banded surfaces into their 0–0.5 µm, 0.5–1 µm and beyond-1 µm rows.

```{python}
#| id: band-analyze-physics
result = resolve_palace_result(RETURNED_RUN_DIR, expected_handoff_id=EXPECTED_HANDOFF_ID)
display(result.show_physics_quantities(ranking_limit=None))
```
